concept.name: Execution simulator
concept.definition: The backtest component that converts hypothetical orders into timestamped fills or rejections under explicit market and brokerage assumptions.
concept.intuition: It is part of the machinery that converts strategy instructions into simulated positions, cash flows, and performance.
concept.mechanics: Apply venue hours, order-type rules, latency, available price and volume, partial-fill logic, costs, and market impact before returning execution events.
concept.failure_modes: Simplified timing, liquidity, fee, borrow, funding, or corporate-action assumptions can make simulated results unattainable live.
concept.misconceptions: A detailed simulator reduces modeling error but cannot reproduce every queue event or future market condition.
concept.example: A 5,000-share market order is capped at 10% of bar volume and fills over several bars with impact.
